summary.headline: Relaxo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8.1% YoY to INR 751 crore, with EBITDA margin at 16.5%, aided partly by GST cut-driven channel restocking.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 751 crore (+8.1% YoY), EBITDA INR 124 crore (+10.6%) and PAT INR 68 crore (+20.4%), with PAT margin at 9.0%. Management attributed the volume recovery to GST cut from 12% to 5%, channel restocking by distributors and better consumer demand, and said the underlying growth is closer to 5-6% over the last two quarters. FY26 revenue fell to INR 2,702 crore from INR 2,790 crore, while PAT rose 5.3% to INR 179 crore. Management has taken 2-3 price increases of roughly 15-18% at consumer level to offset input cost and wage inflation linked to West Asia tensions and Haryana labour costs.

financial_highlights.change: +10.6% YoY; margin vs 16.1% in Q4 FY25
+20.4% YoY vs INR 56 crore; +92 bps margin
+5.3% YoY vs INR 170 crore; vs 6.1% in FY25
up from 550 in previous quarter (per analyst)

segments.name: Brands (FY26 revenue mix)
segments.commentary: Sparx about 40%, Hawaii about 25%, Flite about 35% of revenue across the three major brands, per management.

segments.name: Gender mix
segments.commentary: Men 70%, women 25%, kids 5%; management aims to grow women and kids, currently low.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: About 70,000 retailer/MBO outlets; 420 company-owned EBOs (about 10% of sales per management); presence on e-commerce and quick commerce (Blinkit, Zepto); exports to 37 countries.

guidance_outlook: Operating (EBITDA) margin target for FY27 is about 1% above FY26's 13.8%, i.e. around 14.8%, at company level; management said Q4's margin will not be repeated in full.
Volume growth target of about 4-5% per year over the next two years, per management.
Plans to open 100 new EBOs in FY27: 30-40% in the first half and most by December; each store costs about INR 30-35 lakh.
Ad spend guided at about 4-5% of net sales for FY27, with a shift toward digital.
Management said price increases will not be rolled back as wage costs are unlikely to fall, and said it is too early to guide on price cuts.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR 130 crore; FY27 capex planned at INR 180-200 crore.
Capex is mainly for moulds, one administrative office, wear and tear and machine changes; management said there is no major capacity expansion.
EBO rollout of 100 stores is included within the INR 180-200 crore capex plan.
demand_pricing: Management said the Q4 recovery reflects GST cut from 12% to 5% (distributors carried stock; the pipeline has now largely cleared), with April and May better, and it is too early to call June.
Price increases of about 15-18% blended at consumer level over 2-3 hikes; management said cost inflation is about 15-20% (materials, plus wages of 25-30% in one state and 10-15% in others).
Raw material prices are softening, but labour cost increases are expected to persist.
Management said the company cut trade discounts and lifted contribution on higher volumes, with some benefit from back-end cost work; there was a small price increase in Q4.
Management stated the industry (footwear) is seeing price hikes across players, not only Relaxo; Bata, Red Tape and Metro were cited by analysts as not yet having raised prices.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 growth was a one-off channel restock after the GST cut, and what is underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full impact started after December and underlying growth was about 5-6% over the last two quarters, as distributors' stock was liquidated in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: By how much have input costs risen and how much price has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended consumer price increase of about 15-18%; cost increase estimated at 15-20% including labour, with margins expected to be protected.

qa_highlights.question: Why take price hikes early when competitors have not, and what is the volume risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the April raw material spike and a more than 30% wage increase in Haryana; said the price hike cannot be taken back and gave no volume guidance beyond the 4-5% target.

qa_highlights.question: Does FY27 capex of INR 180-200 crore include the EBO rollout, and will 100 EBOs dilute margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the EBO capex (INR 30-35 lakh per store, about INR 30-35 crore for 100) is part of the INR 200 crore; management said EBO margins are already accretive and company-level margin is expected to rise about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the high Q4 margin, and is there any inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited back-end plant cost reduction, higher volume against fixed costs, lower trade discounts and a small Q4 price increase; denied any inventory gain.

risks_watch: Volume sustainability after 15-18% price hikes, given that a similar 20%+ hike in FY22 hit volumes; management says June is unknown.
Wage inflation in Haryana (above 30% in one state) that management expects to persist, and labour costs elsewhere rising 10-15%.
Price-hike gap versus Bata, Red Tape and Metro, which have not yet announced hikes, as cited by analysts.
Ability to reach 4-5% volume growth against 100 new EBOs and a 25% EBO network expansion, which analysts questioned as inconsistent.
FY26 revenue declined year on year, so the Q4 recovery must be sustained to show full-year growth.
Geopolitical and inflation uncertainty affecting consumer sentiment, which management flagged as not fully visible.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management was confident about Q4 momentum and FY27, but repeatedly qualified guidance by citing geopolitical uncertainty, the unknown demand impact of price hikes and the lack of hard numbers beyond the 1% margin uplift and 4-5% volume goal.

Next 2 years, I think we have to be cautious. Intent is there, again, around, I think, 4% to 5% definitely, we want to grow our volume.

adds.what: 100 new EBOs (company-owned exclusive brand outlets) in FY27, 30-40% in first half, most by December; ~INR 30-35 lakh each

growth.why: Management guides ~4-5% volume growth p.a. for FY27-FY28 and ~1pp higher EBITDA margin (~14.8%), backed by 100 EBO openings within INR 180-200 cr FY27 capex and price hikes of ~15-18%, but no major capacity expansion; the Q4 8.1% revenue jump was partly GST-cut channel restocking, and underlying growth is cited at 5-6%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin about 1pp above FY26's 13.8% (to ~14.8%), backed by 15-18% blended price hikes against 15-20% cost inflation, lower trade discounts and back-end plant cost cuts; management also said Q4's 16.5% will not be repeated in full.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: H1 FY27 start, most of 100 EBOs by December 2026
rows.why: 100 new company-owned EBOs guided for FY27 with 30-40% in H1 and most by December, at INR 30-35 lakh each, within INR 180-200 crore FY27 capex; but management said there is no major manufacturing capacity expansion, so this is retail capacity only.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 4-5% volume growth per year, but underlying growth is only 5-6% over the last two quarters after GST-driven restocking inflated Q4, and 15-18% price hikes raise demand-elasticity risk (a similar 20%+ hike in FY22 hit volumes).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and management said there is no major capacity expansion; FY27 capex of INR 180-200 crore is already planned (mainly moulds, one admin office, EBOs), so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was cautious: it said June is too early to call, gave no guidance beyond the 1pp margin uplift and 4-5% volume goal, and the Q4 lift was partly one-off GST-cut restocking.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Demand after 15-18% price hikes is unproven (June unknown), Haryana wage inflation is above 30%, and analysts questioned whether 4-5% volume growth fits with 100 new EBOs; FY26 revenue already fell to INR 2,702 crore from INR 2,790 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the call covered the existing Sparx, Hawaii and Flite brands and the EBO rollout only.

rows.label: Price hikes not rolled back; no price cuts guided
rows.why: Blended consumer price increase of 15-18% over 2-3 hikes is locked in, with management saying wage costs are unlikely to fall and it is too early to guide on cuts; competitors Bata, Red Tape and Metro had not yet raised prices per analysts.

rows.label: GST-cut distributor pipeline cleared; Q4 restock unwinds
rows.why: Management said distributors carried stock and the pipeline has largely cleared, so the one-off channel restock in Q4's 8.1% revenue growth is unlikely to repeat against underlying growth of 5-6%.

rows.label: Raw material softening vs persistent labour inflation
rows.why: Raw material prices are softening, but labour costs are rising 25-30% in one state and 10-15% in others, with management expecting labour increases to persist against 15-20% total cost inflation.

tone.note: Management was confident about Q4 momentum, the 1pp FY27 margin uplift and the EBO rollout, but qualified everything with the unknown demand response to price hikes and geopolitical risk.
